newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy welcomes OSCE move on Albania peace force.
newsitem.headline: Italy welcomes OSCE move on Albania peace force.

text.p: Italy said on Thursday that the backing of Europe's top security body, the OSCE, for an international protection force for Albania constituted a political endorsement.
"The consensus expressed today by the organisation constitutes the political endorsement for the creation of the multinational protection force," Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said in a statement.

The 54-nation OSCE said after an extraordinary meeting in Vienna that it welcomed an initiative for an international protection force but added that it was up to the United Nations Security Council to give the mission the go ahead.
Italy, which has been flooded by Albanian refugees in recent weeks, said in a statement released there that it would act swiftly to win U.N. backing for the force.
Greece, France, Spain, and Portugal have also said they are prepared to commit troops to Albania. Non-EU members Turkey and Romania have expressed willingness to take part.

Italy has said the military operation would work on the basis of "a minimum use of force" to create a secure environment for international aid organisations working in the crisis-torn Balkan nation and help prepare elections due by June.
Albania was swept by violence in January when a string of popular but fraudulent savings schemes collapsed, swallowing the savings of millions of ordinary people.
Rebels have seized control of the south.
